title: The heartbeat never fires in a session that began with /clear
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-3). Scripts: bin/flux-heartbeat, hooks/hooks.json.

## Context

The heartbeat did not fire once in the session that built FLX-63o. Not late, not
slowly — never, from the first turn to the last.

The evidence is exact. `.flux/session.json` held `last_turn_at 2026-08-13T21:40:59Z`
when the session opened, and the previous session's transcript ends at
`21:40:59.315Z`. That stamp was the *previous* session's closing heartbeat. Across
roughly forty minutes and thirty turns, the only writes to that file were the ones
made by hand. Meanwhile `dirty_files` sat at 0 while the tree carried nine changed
paths, and the statusline read from that same frozen file all session.

What has been ruled out:

- **The script.** Run against a real captured Stop event it stamps correctly and
  exits 0, in 0.9s.
- **The wiring.** A headless `claude -p` in this same repo, no settings override,
  fires it: `last_turn_at` advanced to 22:09:30 and `context_tokens` stamped 28025.
  So `hooks/hooks.json` and the plugin's Stop entry are fine.
- **My own mid-session edit.** The temporary capture hook went in around 21:47, and
  the previous-session stamp proves nothing had fired since 21:41 — the hook was
  already silent before that edit. (Separately confirmed: hooks are snapshotted at
  startup, so that edit could never have taken effect either way.)

What distinguishes this session from the two that work: **it began with `/clear`**.
SessionStart re-fired on it — prime printed its block, so that half of the manifest
is alive — and Stop appears never to have armed. That is the leading hypothesis, not
a conclusion. The cheapest disconfirming check costs nothing: this machine's user
settings play `Glass.aiff` on every Stop. If that sound stops after a `/clear`, no
Stop hook is running and the fault is in the event, not in flux. If it still plays,
the plugin's Stop entry alone is being dropped and the fault is nearer to us.

Why this is P1 rather than a curiosity. Flux's working rule is one ticket per fresh
session (ADR-0003), and `/clear` is how a fresh session is reached. If Stop dies on
clear, the heartbeat is dead in precisely the sessions the harness tells you to work
in — and everything downstream reads stale: the statusline shows a ticket and a drift
count from the session before (AC-4), and `/plan`'s budget notices now read
`context_tokens` from that same frozen file, so FLX-63o's fix reports a real number
belonging to somebody else's window. A stale number is the failure FLX-63o was
written to remove; this would reintroduce it by another route.

Second finding, unrelated to the above and worth its own fix: the installed plugin at
`~/.claude/plugins/cache/flux/flux/0.1.0` is the Aug 10 scaffold. Its `bin/`,
`hooks/`, `skills/` and `agents/` contain nothing but `.gitkeep`, and it has no
`hooks/hooks.json` at all. Everything works today only because the marketplace is a
`directory` source whose installLocation is `/Users/ajmalali/Dev/flux`, so components
resolve from the working tree. If resolution ever prefers `installPath`, every flux
hook disappears silently — the same class of failure as above, with no symptom.

## Tasks

1. Files: (investigation, no edit)
Action: establish whether Stop fires at all after `/clear`. Ask the user whether the
Glass.aiff Stop sound still plays in a cleared session — that alone splits the two
hypotheses. Then reproduce deliberately: open a session, confirm one heartbeat write,
`/clear`, and watch `.flux/session.json` across the next few turns. Fetch current
hook docs for anything said about hook lifetime across `/clear` before concluding.
Verify: two timestamped readings of `.flux/session.json` either side of a `/clear`,
in the same session
Done: the trigger is named, or `/clear` is eliminated and the real one identified

2. Files: hooks/hooks.json, bin/flux-heartbeat (only if task 1 puts the fault here)
Action: fix it if it is ours. If the Stop entry is being dropped for want of a
`matcher` key, or for anything else in the manifest, correct the manifest. If Stop
genuinely does not re-arm after `/clear` and that is upstream, do not invent a
polling mechanism around it — record what is true, file it upstream, and make the
harness degrade honestly instead (see task 3).
Verify: bash tests/run.sh and shellcheck bin/*, plus the task 1 reproduction now
showing a fresh stamp after `/clear`
Done: a cleared session stamps `.flux/session.json` on its next turn

3. Files: bin/flux-statusline, skills/plan/SKILL.md
Action: make staleness visible rather than silent, whatever task 2 concludes. Both
readers currently trust `.flux/session.json` with no sense of its age, and a file
whose writer has stopped is indistinguishable from one written a second ago.
`last_turn_at` is already in the file and is the age. A count or a ticket older than
the current session should read as unknown, not as fact.
Verify: a statusline fixture whose session.json is hours stale, and a /plan budget
read against the same
Done: no reader presents a frozen value as a current one

4. Files: docs/adr/ or CLAUDE.md
Action: record the cache-versus-source resolution finding, so the next person does
not rediscover it at a debugger. One paragraph on where flux@flux actually loads
from and why the cached copy is empty.
Verify: re-read against a fresh `claude plugin validate .claude-plugin/plugin.json`
Done: the hazard is written down where it is read before it bites

## Test plan

The task 1 reproduction is the real test: one session, a heartbeat write, a `/clear`,
another turn, and a second write. `bash tests/run.sh` for the fixtures, `shellcheck
bin/*` if any script changes. AC-3 says the heartbeat writes every turn — this ticket
is what makes that criterion true in the sessions the harness actually runs in.

## Boundaries

Do not work around a dead Stop hook by moving the heartbeat's work into another event
that happens to fire. If Stop is broken, the fix is Stop or an honest degradation, not
a second mechanism doing the same job from a different hook (ADR-0001). Do not touch
the `context_tokens` plumbing FLX-63o just landed — it is correct, and it is a victim
here rather than a cause. Do not reinstall or delete the plugin cache as a fix before
task 1 has named the trigger; that would destroy the evidence.

title: The /plan budget rule reads a status line the model cannot see
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-6). Skill: skills/plan.

## Context

`skills/plan/SKILL.md` step 4 instructs the model to read this session's absolute token
count off the status line at every round boundary:

    The status line carries this session's token count beside `ctx N%` — `83.6k`, `156k`.
    ...Check it at every round boundary, never mid-round.

The model cannot do this. The status line is rendered by `bin/flux-statusline` into the
human's terminal chrome; its output never enters the model's context. A skill instructing
the model to read it is instructing it to read something it has no access to.

Found by the FLX-09 dogfood run (structured-logging spec, zaps/api). All three round
boundaries were reported against an estimate, with the substitution disclosed to the user
each time. The estimate happened to be uncontroversial because the run stayed well under
200k — a run that actually approached either mark would have had a fabricated number
deciding whether to recommend stopping.

This is worse than having no budget rule. AC-6 requires "one notice at 200k and one at
350k", so the acceptance criterion currently tests a behavior the skill cannot perform,
and the prose reads as a safeguard that is not there — the same defect FLX-28 and the
tickets commit b447180 removed elsewhere.

Two viable directions, and choosing between them is the substance of this ticket:

- **Deliver the count to the model.** Prime already injects state at SessionStart, but
  budget marks need checking mid-session at every round boundary, and no hook fires there.
  The Stop heartbeat runs every turn and could stamp the count into `.flux/session.json`,
  which the skill could then read — cheap, deterministic, and consistent with ADR-0001.
  Whether the count is available to the hook at all needs checking before this is chosen.
- **Rewrite the rule to what the model can actually do.** Say "estimate" and drop the
  precision, or reframe the marks as round counts rather than token counts. Cheaper, and
  weaker.

## Tasks

1. Files: (investigation, no edit)
   Action: establish whether the Stop hook's event JSON carries a usable token or context
   figure. Fetch current Claude Code hook docs first — do not answer from memory (house
   rule). Record the answer in this ticket's notes; it decides task 2.
   Verify: `bash -c 'echo "$FIXTURE" | bin/flux-heartbeat'` against a real captured Stop
   event, showing which fields are present
   Done: the field is named, or its absence is established

2. Files: skills/plan/SKILL.md, and bin/flux-heartbeat + bin/flux-statusline if task 1
   found a usable field
   Action: make the budget rule performable. If the count is reachable, stamp it into
   `.flux/session.json` and have step 4 read it from there. If it is not, rewrite step 4
   so it asks only for what the model can do, and stop claiming a precision that is not
   available.
   Verify: `shellcheck bin/*` and `bash tests/run.sh`, plus a live `/plan` round boundary
   where the reported figure is traceable to its source
   Done: no instruction in the skill asks the model to read the status line

3. Files: specs/harness/spec.md
   Action: bring AC-6 into line with whatever task 2 settled, so the acceptance criterion
   describes a checkable behavior.
   Verify: re-read AC-6 against the revised skill
   Done: AC-6 and the skill agree

## Test plan

A live `/plan` run reaching at least two round boundaries, confirming the reported budget
figure comes from a named source rather than a guess. `bash tests/run.sh` and `shellcheck`
if any bin script changed.

## Boundaries

Do not add a hook that fires per round — there is no such event, and inventing a polling
mechanism for this is out of proportion. The heartbeat already runs every turn. Do not
change the 200k/350k values or their advisory nature; FLX-30 settled that and this ticket
is only about whether the numbers can be observed at all.
notes:
Task 1 — settled: the Stop hook event carries NO token or context figure.

Real captured Stop event (headless 'claude -p' with hook 'cat > stop-event.json'), full field list:
  session_id, transcript_path, cwd, prompt_id, permission_mode, hook_event_name,
  stop_hook_active, last_assistant_message, background_tasks, session_crons
A path-scan for token|context|usage|window over that JSON returns NONE. The current hooks
docs agree: the common-input table has no context_window, and Stop adds only
stop_hook_active and last_assistant_message.

But the count IS reachable, one hop away. transcript_path is a common field, and the
transcript JSONL carries per-message usage — input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens,
cache_read_input_tokens, output_tokens — on every assistant record. Their sum on the last
main-thread record is the same quantity the statusline prints (its context_window totals
are input inclusive of cache reads and writes). Measured: tail -c 400k | jq = 9ms, well
inside the 500ms budget.

Two caveats, both tolerable: the docs say the transcript is written asynchronously and may
lag the in-memory conversation, so the stamp is as of the last completed turn; and
sidechain records (subagents) must be filtered out or a scout's window pollutes the count.

Decision: take the first direction — stamp it into .flux/session.json from the heartbeat
and have step 4 read it there.

Incidental finding worth keeping: a hook config change does not take effect mid-session.
Hooks are snapshotted at startup, which is why the capture had to come from a separate
headless session rather than from this one.

title: PR bodies are filled by the agent, opened by a script
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (further notes — no AC yet; this ticket needs a spec pass first).

## Context
The same split as FLX-<commit>, one level up: the agent fills a PR template and nothing
else, and a script runs `gh pr create --body-file`. Deferred rather than built, because
flux has no branch or PR workflow today — this repo commits directly to main, there is no
`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, and no skill owns the ship step. Building the script
first would invent the workflow it is meant to serve.

Open before this can be written: which repo the flow is for (flux itself, or the zaps
repos where PRs actually happen); whether the template is the target repo's or one flux
ships; and where the branch comes from, since one-ticket-per-session says nothing about
branching yet.

## Tasks
1. Files: (none — spec first)
   Action: run /flux:plan on the ship step, ending at a spec that answers the three open
   questions above. Then /flux:tickets in a fresh window.
   Verify: specs/<slug>/spec.md exists and is approved
   Done: this ticket is replaced by the tickets that spec produces

## Test plan
None yet — the spec decides it.

## Boundaries
Write no script until the spec exists. Do not create a PR template in this repo on the
assumption it will be wanted.
notes: ADR-0011 gives the spec pass its vocabulary: prose slot under .flux/, hook trigger, script validates form and performs the act. The PR body is the second instance of the pattern, so it should call bin/flux-common rather than re-invent FLX-a4g's slot handling.

title: bd close commits the ticket, from a message the agent only writes
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-8). ADR-0001, ADR-0002. CLAUDE.md working rule.

## Context
CLAUDE.md already says a ticket closes with a commit naming its id. Today the agent does
that by hand, which spends tokens on a mechanical act and lets unrelated edits ride along
— FLX-10's session had a CLAUDE.md change sitting in the tree beside it. The split this
ticket builds: the agent writes the message text and nothing else; a script stages, commits
and reports.

The staging rule is the hard part. A ticket's `Files:` lines are prose, not a manifest —
real examples include `(investigation, no edit)`, `docs/adr/ or CLAUDE.md`, and
`hooks/hooks.json, bin/flux-heartbeat (only if task 1 puts the fault here)`. So the script
extracts path-shaped tokens and intersects them with what git reports as actually changed.
The intersection is the safety: prose tokens match no changed path, directory tokens match
what changed beneath them, and a file the ticket named too vaguely is left dirty and
printed rather than swept in.

## Tasks
1. Files: bin/flux-commit
   Action: PostToolUse hook on Bash. Act only when the command was a `bd close <id>` that
   succeeded. Read `.flux/commit-msg`, validate the format (subject `<TICKET-ID>: <text>`
   at most 72 chars, blank second line, body wrapped, Co-Authored-By trailer), derive the
   staging set as described in Context, commit, and delete the message file. Print what was
   staged and what was left dirty. Exit 0 on every path.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: a fixture repo with a dirty tree and a valid message produces exactly one commit
   containing only the intersected paths (AC-8)
2. Files: bin/flux-guard
   Action: extend the guard so `bd close` is denied when `.flux/commit-msg` is absent or
   malformed AND the ticket's files have uncommitted changes — the deny reason carries the
   format. A close with nothing to commit (investigation tickets, /sync retroactive closes)
   is allowed with no message.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: both branches covered by fixtures
3. Files: skills/tickets/ticket-template.md
   Action: state that `Files:` names real paths — no prose, no alternatives, no ticket ids
   — because a script stages from it. Existing prose lines stay readable by the
   intersection, but new tickets should not need it.
   Verify: read back
   Done: the rule is stated where tickets are written
4. Files: tests/
   Action: fixtures for valid message, malformed message, nothing-to-commit, and a dirty
   file outside the ticket's Files.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: cases pass, shellcheck clean

## Test plan
Fixture git repos built in a temp dir, asserted on `git log` and `git status` output.
Live verification is next-session only (hooks snapshot at startup).

## Boundaries
Commits only — never pushes, never touches a branch, never amends. The message is the
agent's; the script must not compose or edit prose beyond validating its shape.
notes: ADR-0011 names the pattern this ticket builds and rejects beads formulas/mol/gate as an alternative (they template ticket graphs; nothing in them executes). Two consequences for task 1: the slot read, form validation and 'staged X / left Y dirty' reporting belong in bin/flux-common, not inline, because FLX-0jn is the second caller. And the Files: intersection is documented there as a compensation for a script that cannot judge — scriptify the act, never the decision.

title: Guard hook: beads reads carry --json, and the agent never runs git commit
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-5, AC-13, AC-14). ADR-0001, ADR-0002, ADR-0004.

## Context
Two rules that prompts cannot hold. The first: every beads read passes `--json`, because
the human-readable output is a rendering clipped to terminal width, so a ticket body read
out of it is the body as displayed rather than as stored. `bin/flux-common` already reads
this way; the breakage is always a hand-typed command. The second: the agent never runs
`git commit`, `git push`, or `git commit --amend` itself — the commit is machinery
(FLX-a4g), and the agent's only contribution is the message text.

Both are PreToolUse denials on Bash, which is a real departure: every hook flux ships so
far fails open (ADR-0001), and a guard that fails open is not a guard.

That departure decides how they ship. State hooks (prime, heartbeat) are plugin-scoped in
`hooks/hooks.json` and active for anyone who installs flux, which is safe because they
only stamp a JSON file. A fail-closed deny cannot arrive that way — someone who installed
flux for the status line would find `git commit` blocked by a plugin update they did not
read. So the scripts ship in `bin/` with the plugin, and `/flux:init` wires them into the
target repo's `.claude/settings.json` on request, the way `gitnexus-reindex` is already
wired in this repo. Opt-in per repo, declinable, and visible in the init report.

## Tasks
1. Files: bin/flux-guard
   Action: PreToolUse hook on Bash. Deny (a) a `bd` invocation that reads (show/list/ready
   /dep list/stats) without `--json`, (b) `git commit`, `git push`, `git commit --amend`,
   `git reset --hard`. Emit the documented JSON: hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName
   "PreToolUse", permissionDecision "deny", permissionDecisionReason naming the corrected
   command. Exit 0 on every path so a malformed event never blocks a legitimate call, and
   allow silently (no output) when nothing matches.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: fixture events for each denied shape produce the exact deny JSON, and an allowed
   shape produces empty stdout (AC-5)
2. Files: skills/init/SKILL.md
   Action: a new optional checklist item — "guard hooks" — that merges a PreToolUse entry
   for bin/flux-guard into the repo's `.claude/settings.json`, after asking. States both
   what it blocks and how to remove it. Declining is a first-class outcome: `[declined]`,
   and the rest of the checklist continues. A second run is a no-op. Fetch the current hook
   schema before writing the JSON — do not write field names from memory (CLAUDE.md).
   Verify: run /flux:init on a scratch repo twice
   Done: first run offers and wires it, second run reports [exists] and writes nothing
   (AC-13)
3. Files: hooks/hooks.json
   Action: nothing. Named here so the boundary is explicit — the guard is deliberately not
   registered plugin-side, and a later session must not "fix" its absence.
   Verify: git diff --exit-code hooks/hooks.json
   Done: unchanged, and the reason is in the ADR
4. Files: docs/adr/00NN-guard-hooks-fail-closed.md
   Action: the ADR. ADR-0001 says hooks fail open; a deny hook fails closed by design.
   Name the split — state hooks plugin-scoped and fail-open, guard hooks project-scoped,
   opt-in and fail-closed — and the cost accepted: a broken guard blocks legitimate work,
   which is why its every path exits 0 and it denies only on a positive match.
   Verify: read it back against ADR-0001 and ADR-0004
   Done: ADR exists, ADR-0001 is not silently contradicted
5. Files: tests/
   Action: fixtures + cases for each deny shape and one allow shape, following the existing
   fixture layout.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: cases pass, shellcheck clean

## Test plan
Fixture JSON piped to stdin with exact-output assertions, the pattern tests/ already uses.
Live verification is next-session only: hooks are snapshotted at startup, so a hook added
during a session is not active in it.

## Boundaries
Denial only — this ticket never performs a commit. What happens after a denial is FLX-a4g.
Do not widen the git denials beyond the four named; a guard that blocks `git add` or
`git status` makes the harness unusable. Do not register the guard in hooks/hooks.json.
notes: ADR-0011 (docs/adr/0011-the-agent-supplies-prose-scripts-perform-the-act.md) names the pattern this ticket enforces: the agent supplies prose, a script performs the act. The guard is that ADR's enforcement leg — it says so explicitly. Task 4's ADR stays separate and narrower: why a guard hook may fail closed when ADR-0001 says fail open.

title: An abandoned /plan run leaves nothing — only a called pause is cheap
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-6, AC-10). Skill: skills/plan. Related: FLX-25.

## Context

`/plan` promises two endings and no third: an approved spec, or a draft plus a handoff.
There is a third, and the FLX-09 dogfood hit it — the window was closed mid-run.

The run had asked round 1's five questions and both scouts had returned ~100k tokens of
findings. Nothing had settled yet, so by the skill's own rule no draft existed; the run
was closed rather than paused, so no handoff was written either. What survived on disk was
an empty `specs/structured-logging/` directory. Everything else — the questions, the scout
findings, the reasoning — existed only in the transcript.

It was recovered, but only by reading `~/.claude/projects/*/`*`.jsonl` by hand and
reconstructing the round from the raw turns. That is luck, not design: the transcript is
host state that the harness does not own, does not reference anywhere, and cannot rely on.

The skill's own logic is not at fault. "The draft appears the round the first section
settles" is correct, and a closed terminal cannot be intercepted. What is wrong is the
claim: "Two endings, and no third: an approved spec, or a draft with a handoff beside it.
A run that produces neither is still running." A run that produces neither is frequently
just dead, and the harness currently has no way to tell the difference — prime surfaces
handoffs, and there is no handoff.

The cheapness of a pause is real but only applies to a *called* pause. The expensive part
of a planning run is front-loaded: the scouts run in round 1, before anything can possibly
have settled, so the window in which an abandoned run loses the most is exactly the window
in which the skill has deposited the least.

Options, and picking one is the work:

- **Deposit at slug time.** Write a stub the moment the slug settles — the input idea and
  the opening frontier — so an abandoned run leaves a readable trace. Costs one write per
  run and slightly weakens "the draft is only settled sections".
- **Deposit scout findings when they land**, not when they settle a section. They are facts
  rather than decisions, which is a different kind of content from the rest of the draft.
- **Accept it and fix the claim.** Say plainly that an abandoned run loses the round in
  progress, and stop asserting there is no third ending.

## Tasks

1. Files: skills/plan/SKILL.md
   Action: settle which of the three options above holds, and make the "Done" section
   truthful about it. If a deposit-early option is chosen, say exactly what gets written
   and when; the file it writes must not be mistaken for a settled draft.
   Verify: live `/plan` run abandoned deliberately after round 1, then a fresh session in
   the same repo — inspect what a reader can recover with no transcript access
   Done: what survives an abandoned run is stated in the skill and matches what actually
   survives

2. Files: skills/plan/SKILL.md
   Action: whatever is chosen, an empty `specs/<slug>/` must not be the only artifact —
   either it carries something, or it is not created until it does (see the sibling ticket
   on premature directory creation, which this may subsume).
   Verify: `ls specs/` after a deliberately abandoned run
   Done: no directory exists whose only content is its own name

## Test plan

Abandon a `/plan` run after round 1 in a sandbox repo, then open a fresh session and
attempt to resume from disk alone, with the transcript treated as unavailable. The test is
whether the next session can tell that a run happened and what it was about.

## Boundaries

Do not build transcript recovery into the harness — the transcript is host state, its
format is not ours, and depending on it would be a worse dependency than the gap it
closes. Do not touch the pause path itself; FLX-25 owns residue and handoff format, and
this ticket must not fork a second definition of either.

title: prime's drift line names both endings, not just /sync
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-1, AC-11). ADR-0007.

## Context
Prime's drift sentence read `N commits not linked to tickets — run /sync when convenient.`
That names one legal ending out of two. Committing outside the harness on purpose is not a
defect, and a user who says "leave those alone" is answering the question rather than
refusing it — but the line gave that answer no words and, worse, no effect: with nothing
advancing `last_synced_commit`, a declined drift returns at the same count every session,
which is how a warning teaches you to ignore it (the reasoning ADR-0006 already applied to
the statusline).

The wording half lands here. The mechanism half is FLX-14's: `/sync --skip` advances the
baseline past the accepted commits without creating tickets, and `last_synced_commit` keeps
its single writer. Shipping the offer without the mechanism would have been the same empty
safeguard FLX-27 and FLX-28 were about, so the two halves are written to agree.

## Tasks
1. Files: bin/flux-prime, tests/fixtures/prime/drift/expected.txt, tests/fixtures/prime/drift-one/expected.txt
   Action: name both endings in the drift sentence, singular and plural, and update the two
   fixtures that assert it verbatim.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: both drift fixtures pass against the new wording; suite green
2. Files: FLX-14 (beads body)
   Action: give /sync the `--skip` path so the offer is honoured — confirm first, print the
   commits being accepted, run only the listing and baseline steps, and state that the
   baseline now asserts "accounted for" rather than "ticketed". Drift accrued afterwards
   still counts.
   Verify: FLX-14 names --skip in its flow, its Done, its test plan and its boundaries
   Done: no instruction anywhere offers a skip that nothing implements

## Test plan
The two prime fixtures. The live half cannot run until FLX-14 ships: two raw commits,
`/sync --skip`, drift zero next session with `bd list` unchanged, then a third raw commit
counting as 1 rather than 3.

## Boundaries
Wording and ticket text only — no change to `drift_count`, to `last_synced_commit`, or to
which component may write it. Do not implement `/sync` here; FLX-14 owns the skill.

title: gitnexus index refreshes itself when HEAD moves
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (Further notes — gitnexus stays optional). ADR-0001.

## Context
gitnexus ships a PostToolUse hook that only reports staleness: `gitnexus-hook.cjs:191`
says it avoids spawning `analyze` because a synchronous run blocks the tool call. The
notice therefore arrives every turn after a commit and costs a manual `npx gitnexus
analyze` to clear. Claude Code's `async: true` removes the blocking objection, so the
fix can run itself.

Deliberately **not** shipped in flux's `hooks/hooks.json`. Doing so would make gitnexus a
de-facto default for every repo that adopts flux, and the spec keeps that indexing
optional until the PolyForm licence question is settled. It lives in this repo's
`.claude/settings.json` instead, where it binds nobody else.

## Tasks
1. Files: .claude/hooks/gitnexus-reindex, .claude/settings.json
   Action: Stop hook, `async: true`, guarded on `.gitnexus/meta.json` — reindex only when
   `lastCommit` differs from HEAD, and never index a repo that has no index (opting in
   stays the user's call). Re-pass `--embeddings` when the existing index had them, or the
   refresh silently drops them. mkdir lock so two quick commits do not run two analyzes,
   with a 10-minute staleness escape so a killed run cannot wedge it for good. Fail-open
   throughout (ADR-0001).
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh; run the hook with HEAD == indexed and confirm meta.json is untouched
   Done: no-op path is well inside the 500ms budget; every failure path exits 0
2. Files: tests/run.sh
   Action: extend the shellcheck suite over `.claude/hooks/*` — not a shipped component,
   but it runs on every Stop here and the shell contract applies to it the same.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: the script is shellchecked by the suite

## Test plan
Measured no-op path (HEAD == indexed, meta.json unchanged). Fail-open edges: not a git
repo, git repo with no `.gitnexus/`, malformed meta.json, malformed stdin — all exit 0,
and the malformed case leaks no lock.

## Boundaries
Repo-local only: nothing added to hooks/hooks.json, plugin.json, or the flux bin/. Do not
make flux depend on gitnexus while the licence question is open — if shipping it ever
becomes the right call, that is an ADR and a spec edit, not an edit to this hook.
notes: gitnexus analyze rewrites prose by default: it appends a ~100-line section to CLAUDE.md and writes AGENTS.md beside it. Caught on the first live run — the reindex dirtied CLAUDE.md, which a hook firing on every HEAD move would then redo after every commit. --skip-agents-md suppresses both and is mandatory in this hook, not a preference. The injected text is also wrong for this repo: it mandates an impact query before editing any symbol, against a graph with 0 execution flows, which is the opposite of the minimal-context rule in FLX-11. Verified by a forced full reanalyze leaving CLAUDE.md byte-identical and creating no AGENTS.md.

title: Decide whether docs/architecture.md exists
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-8, AC-11). Blocks FLX-11 and FLX-14.

## Context
`docs/architecture.md` does not exist. Two unbuilt tickets instruct an agent to reconcile
against it:

- FLX-11 (f): "check the diff against docs/architecture.md and ADRs — update or flag"
- FLX-14 (d): "check the combined changes against docs/architecture.md, docs/adr/, and
  CONTEXT.md: update architecture.md for structural changes"

Nothing in any ticket creates it, and nothing says what it contains. An agent told to
reconcile against a missing file will most likely note nothing and continue — the
instruction reads as a safeguard while having no mechanism behind it, which is the same
failure shape as FLX-27.

It is also absent from the sanctioned list. The house rule in CLAUDE.md says durable
knowledge lives "only in `CONTEXT.md`, `docs/adr/`, `specs/`, or this file". A maintained
architecture document is not among them, so either the list is wrong or the two tickets
are.

This is a decision, not an implementation. Three answers are live:

(a) **It exists**, and /build and /sync maintain it. Buys a real structural check; costs a
    fourth durable document with a currency problem — a structure doc nobody reads goes
    stale, and a stale one does not fail silently, it asserts things that are false.
(b) **It does not exist.** Both tickets drop the reference, and the close-time check runs
    against ADRs and CONTEXT.md only, which are decisions and vocabulary rather than
    structure. Cheapest; leaves structural drift genuinely undetected.
(c) **gitnexus supplies it on demand.** Structure is computed rather than maintained, which
    is what gitnexus is for and it is already indexed against this repo. No document to go
    stale; costs a dependency on an external index in the close path, and says nothing when
    the index is stale — as it is right now.

## Tasks
1. Files: docs/adr/00NN-*.md
   Action: settle it and record the decision at the ADR bar — this is hard to reverse once
   tickets are written against it, and each option trades a real thing away. State which of
   (a)/(b)/(c) holds and why the other two lose.
   Verify: the ADR names the losing options and what each would have bought
   Done: an ADR exists that a future ticket can cite instead of assuming

2. Files: FLX-11, FLX-14 (beads bodies)
   Action: correct both to match the decision — either architecture.md is real and
   something creates it, or the references go. If (a), this ticket also has to say what
   writes the file first, since neither skill can update a document that does not exist.
   Verify: grep -r 'architecture.md' returns only intentional references
   Done: no ticket instructs a check against a file whose existence is undecided

## Test plan
Mostly a reading check — grep for the string and confirm every hit is deliberate. If (a)
wins, the real test is FLX-11's live run: /build's close step must actually update the file
rather than report that it did.

## Boundaries
Do not write docs/architecture.md as part of settling this — that presumes (a). If (a)
wins, creating and seeding the file is its own ticket with its own verify. Do not widen
this into a review of what else belongs in the durable-knowledge list; the CLAUDE.md house
rule is evidence here, not scope.

title: The ADR access rule cannot be followed
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-13). ADR-0003.

## Context
`skills/init/claude-md-section.md` tells every repo that adopts flux:

    Decisions: `docs/adr/` — read before changing anything they cover

That cannot be followed. Knowing whether an ADR covers your change requires reading it,
so the instruction demands its own outcome as a precondition. At 9 ADRs (113 lines total)
it degrades into "read them all", which is cheap and roughly correct. At 40 it degrades
into ignoring the rule, while the rule stays on the page implying compliance.

It also contradicts the harness. FLX-11's minimal-context rule deliberately excludes ADRs
from what /build loads — "the ticket, the spec section it names, CONTEXT.md, gitnexus
`context` on symbols the ticket names — and nothing else until a task demands it" — and
reads them only at close, against a finished diff. That is the right access pattern and
it is already designed; only the prose disagrees with it.

The convention that makes selective reading work already exists: ADR filenames state their
decisions as sentences (`0007-prime-speaks-to-the-model-the-statusline-speaks-to-the-human`),
so `ls docs/adr/` is an index costing ~60 tokens. Nothing writes that down.

This is a template, not a local wording fix. Editing CLAUDE.md alone is reverted by the
next `/flux:init`, which is idempotent by AC-13 and rewrites the block.

## Tasks
1. Files: skills/init/claude-md-section.md
   Action: replace the Decisions line with an access pattern an agent can execute —
   `ls docs/adr/` to route by filename, open only what the change touches, check the
   finished diff against them at close. Match FLX-11's load/close split rather than
   implying ADRs are read up front.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: no instruction requires reading an ADR to learn whether it should be read

2. Files: CLAUDE.md
   Action: apply the same replacement in both places it appears — the house "Where things
   live" list, and the generated `<!-- flux -->` block, which must match the template
   byte-for-byte or /flux:init will rewrite it on the next run.
   Verify: re-run /flux:init and confirm the block is unchanged (AC-13 idempotence)
   Done: both copies agree with the template and with each other

## Test plan
The idempotence check in task 2 is the real test — a fix that /flux:init reverts is not a
fix. Edge: a repo with no `docs/adr/` at all, where the instruction must still read
sensibly rather than sending an agent after a missing directory.

## Boundaries
Wording only. Do not add ADR frontmatter, scope tags, or an index file — the filenames
already carry that and the corpus is 113 lines; the machinery pays off somewhere near 40
ADRs and not before. Do not change FLX-11's close step, which is already correct.

title: TICKET_ID_RE misses beads-generated ids
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md. ADR-0002, ADR-0006.

## Context
`bin/flux-common:17` hardcodes `TICKET_ID_RE='FLX-[0-9]+|bd-[a-z0-9]+'`. That matched the
markdown store, whose ids were hand-numbered `FLX-01..FLX-25`, and it still matches every
imported ticket. It does not match the ids beads generates on its own: `bd init` reports
"Issues will be named: FLX-<hash> (e.g. FLX-a3f2dd)". The imported tickets all carry
explicit numeric ids, so nothing is broken today — the first ticket created by `/tickets`
through `bd create` without `--id` is the one that breaks.

Two consumers fail on that id, both in `bin/flux-common`:

- line 141, the drift counter — a commit naming `FLX-a3f2dd` does not match, so a properly
  linked commit is counted as drift. The statusline nags about work that was tracked.
- line 340, `store_done` — the commit-to-ticket match never fires, so the beads path falls
  through to its own ordering.

Related, and deliberately not a ticket: the bulk import stamped all 17 closed tickets with
the same `closed_at`, so ADR-0006's "beads has genuine close timestamps and sorts on them"
has nothing to sort. The idle statusline currently reads `FLX-24-done` where the markdown
path said `FLX-08`. This self-corrects on the first real `bd close`.

## Tasks
1. Files: bin/flux-common
   Action: widen `TICKET_ID_RE` to admit beads' generated ids alongside the numeric ones.
   The prefix is per-repo (`bd init -p <PREFIX>`), so prefer a prefix-agnostic pattern over
   hardcoding `FLX`; read the prefix from `.beads/config.yaml` only if a pattern cannot do
   it inside the statusline's 100ms budget (ADR-0004 forbids a store verb there).
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: a commit naming a hash id is not counted as drift, and `store_done` matches it

2. Files: tests/
   Action: fixtures covering both id shapes — numeric `FLX-09` and generated `FLX-a3f2dd` —
   through the drift counter and `store_done`.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: both shapes asserted; suite green

## Test plan
The fixtures in task 2. Edge: a commit message containing a bare word that looks like a
prefix (`FLX-` with no id) must not match. Edge: repo whose prefix is not `FLX`.

## Boundaries
`bin/flux-common` only — no change to the store verbs' contract or to what the statusline
is allowed to run. Do not renumber or re-id any existing ticket.

title: flux ships its own copies of the skills it composes
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (implementation decisions, Skills bullet — this ticket amends it).

## Context
Flux skills compose five skills that today live in the `mattpocock-skills` plugin: grilling
and domain-modeling and prototype (invoked by /plan), tdd (invoked by /build), and
codebase-design (referenced from tdd's own body). Nothing makes a user have them. The
manifest answer — a `dependencies` entry naming `mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official`
plus `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn` in our marketplace — works, but it disables the
entire harness with `dependency-unsatisfied` whenever the dependency is missing or its
marketplace was never added. Carrying our own copies removes the failure mode and lets flux
own the conventions domain-modeling writes into, which are the same CONTEXT.md and
docs/adr/ this harness already has opinions about. Upstream is MIT, © 2026 Matt Pocock.

Verbatim copies in this ticket. Reconciling their vocabulary with CONTEXT.md is later work,
and it stays legible only if the copies start out diffable against upstream.

## Tasks
1. Files: docs/adr/0009-companion-skills-are-vendored.md
   Action: record the reversal — flux ships copies rather than depending on the plugin.
   State the rejected alternative (cross-marketplace `dependencies`) with the reason it
   loses: an unresolved dependency disables prime, heartbeat, statusline and every skill,
   not just the one that needed it. State the accepted cost: upstream improvements arrive
   only through a deliberate re-sync, and nothing reminds us.
   Verify: `ls docs/adr/0009-*`
   Done: ADR carries decision, rejected alternative, and accepted cost.
2. Files: specs/harness/spec.md
   Action: rewrite the Skills bullet under implementation decisions. Skills are composed by
   reference and never restated inside another skill's body — that rule stands. What changes
   is where the composed skills come from: this plugin, per ADR-0009.
   Verify: `grep -rn 'installed mattpocock-skills' specs/` returns nothing
   Done: no line in specs/ tells a skill to invoke something flux does not ship.
3. Files: skills/grilling/, skills/domain-modeling/, skills/prototype/, skills/tdd/,
   skills/codebase-design/, skills/NOTICE.md
   Action: copy each directory byte-for-byte from mattpocock-skills 1.2.3, sibling
   reference files and `agents/openai.yaml` included, so a future re-sync is a diff rather
   than a reconstruction. Frontmatter `name` keeps its upstream value; the skills resolve
   as `flux:<name>`. NOTICE.md carries the MIT licence text, the copyright line, the
   upstream version each copy came from, and the command that fetches a newer one.
   Verify: `claude plugin validate .claude-plugin/plugin.json`, then `/reload-plugins`
   Done: five skills load under the flux namespace; NOTICE.md names version 1.2.3.
4. Files: skills/plan/SKILL.md
   Action: repoint the three invocations from `mattpocock-skills:<name>` to `flux:<name>`.
   Verify: `grep -rn 'mattpocock-skills' skills/` matches only NOTICE.md
   Done: /plan invokes only skills this plugin ships.

## Test plan
Task 3's verify, then the real proof: `claude plugin disable
mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official`, open a fresh session, run /flux:plan far enough
to reach the first grilling round. It reaches it. Re-enable afterwards. Edge: both plugins
enabled at once — two `grilling` skills exist, namespaces keep them apart, and /plan reaches
the flux one.

## Boundaries
No edits to the vendored bodies. They still say `/codebase-design` and `/prototype` in
their own voice and still describe CONTEXT.md in their own format; reconciling that with
this repo's glossary is a separate ticket and a separate commit. Do not add a
`dependencies` entry to plugin.json. Do not vendor the other twenty skills in that plugin —
only what a flux skill actually invokes.

title: The status line names the verb, but only when there is one to name
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-4), ADR-0007.

## Context
The line reports state accurately and leaves the reader to know what to do about
it. `⚠ 2 drift` assumes you remember that /sync is the answer; a window at 78%
assumes you think to pause before it costs you the session. The harness has the
verbs, so the line can name one.

It names at most one, and only when there is something to act on — the same rule
that keeps the drift segment off the line the rest of the time. A hint that is
always present is furniture, and furniture is not read. Priority is by cost of
inaction: a full context window loses the session, drift only loses
attribution.

    FLX-06-claimed · main · ctx 78% · 140k · /pause
    FLX-21-done · main · ⚠ 2 drift · ctx 41% · 82.4k · /sync
    FLX-06-claimed · main · ctx 41% · 82.4k

Both verbs are unbuilt (FLX-13, FLX-14). Naming them anyway is deliberate and
already the precedent — prime's block has said "run /sync when convenient" since
FLX-02. The pluralisation added in FLX-22 comes back out at the same time:
`drift` is the condition the commits add up to, and it does not take an -s.

## Tasks
1. Files: bin/flux-statusline
   Action: append ` · <verb>` when a condition warrants one — context at or over
   HINT_CTX_PCT → /pause, else drift → /sync, else nothing. Arithmetic only: no
   new file reads, no forks, both inputs are already in hand.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh statusline
   Done: hint present only under those conditions, and never two at once
2. Files: tests/fixtures/statusline/
   Action: cases for each hint, for the priority order when both fire, and the
   silence of the steady state. Retarget the two drift fixtures, which now end
   in the verb.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: every existing case still renders unchanged apart from those two
3. Files: README.md, specs/harness/spec.md
   Action: document the rule, not the list — the list will grow with the skills.
   Verify: grep for `drifts` returns nothing outside FLX-22's own record
   Done: AC-4 describes hints and the plural is gone everywhere

## Test plan
The steady-state case is the one that matters: two existing fixtures already
assert a line with no hint, and they must not move.

## Boundaries
No new reads in the statusline (FLX-04): a hint that needs data the hooks have
not already stamped is a hint for a later ticket. Unconsumed handoffs are the
obvious next candidate and are deliberately left out — no verb consumes one yet,
and pointing at a verb we have not chosen is the guessing ADR-0006 removed.

title: Drift is visible to the human, not only to the model
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-1, AC-4, AC-5).

## Context
Found running FLX-05's check 4. Prime's drift line is a nudge — "N commits not
linked to tickets, run /sync" — addressed to a human who cannot see it. Claude
Code adds SessionStart stdout to the model's context and does not render it in
the terminal (hooks docs, exit-code-0 table, re-read 2026-08-11), which is
confirmed in this repo's own transcripts: the block arrives as a `hook_success`
attachment and never reaches the screen. The warning therefore fires only if the
model happens to mention it, which is the one thing a deterministic hook was
supposed to stop depending on.

The human's surface is the statusline. It already carries what is true right now
and nothing else, so drift belongs there — but only when there is drift, so the
common case stays as clean as it is today:

    FLX-20-done · main · ctx 41% · 83.6k
    FLX-20-done · main · ⚠ 2 drift · ctx 41% · 83.6k

Counting it there is out of the question: that is a git log per keystroke. The
count is resolved in the hooks, exactly as the ticket is (ADR-0006), and the
statusline only reads the number. Prime already computes it; the heartbeat must
learn to, so the count stays fresh across a session in which commits are made.

## Tasks
1. Files: bin/flux-common, bin/flux-prime
   Action: move `collect_drift` (and MAX_DRIFT_SCAN) into flux-common as
   `drift_count <root>`, returning a number and 0 whenever there is no usable
   baseline. Prime keeps printing its sentence from the same value.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh prime
   Done: prime/drift still passes unchanged
2. Files: bin/flux-common, bin/flux-heartbeat, bin/flux-prime
   Action: add `drift_commits` to SESSION_KEYS as a second numeric field; both
   hooks stamp it. The baseline itself stays untouched — only /sync moves it.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh heartbeat
   Done: session.json carries a live count after every turn
3. Files: bin/flux-statusline
   Action: render `⚠ N drift` between the branch and the ctx segment when the
   count is above zero, and nothing at all when it is zero or unreadable. Needs
   a numeric read for the no-jq path, where the existing sed_field only matches
   quoted values.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh statusline
   Done: segment appears only when there is drift, jq or no jq
4. Files: tests/fixtures/{statusline,heartbeat}/
   Action: a statusline case with drift and one proving zero renders nothing; a
   heartbeat case pinning the stamped count against a real baseline.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: all suites green

## Test plan
The zero case matters as much as the non-zero one — a warning segment that is
always present is a warning nobody reads. Every existing statusline fixture is
already a zero case and must render exactly as before.

## Boundaries
No git and no store verb in the statusline (FLX-04). Do not touch
`last_synced_commit` (FLX-14 owns it). Do not change prime's sentence — the
model reads it, and it is the thing /sync will act on.

title: Prime asks for a relay, and the counts read as English
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-1, AC-4), ADR-0007.

## Context
Two things, both from watching FLX-21 land.

The counts do not agree with their nouns: `⚠ 1 drift` is right and `⚠ 2 drift`
is not, and prime says "1 commits not linked to tickets". Small, but this is the
line the human reads every second of every session, and broken agreement is what
makes a tool feel unmaintained.

Second, ADR-0007 says the primed block is invisible to the human and concludes
that anything needing human action goes to the status line. That holds for
standing state, but it leaves the block itself unread by anyone but the model —
and the block carries things the status line has no room for, handoffs above
all. Prime can close that gap itself: it writes into the model's context, so it
can ask the model to relay. One line, at the top of the first reply, naming only
what needs a person. Note the ceiling honestly — Claude Code produces no turn
before the user types, so the relay lands atop the answer to the first prompt,
not on the empty screen.

## Tasks
1. Files: bin/flux-statusline, bin/flux-prime
   Action: agree the noun with the count — `⚠ 1 drift` / `⚠ 2 drifts`, and
   "1 commit not linked to tickets" / "2 commits not linked to tickets".
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh statusline prime
   Done: both singular and plural pinned by fixtures
2. Files: bin/flux-prime
   Action: close the block with one line asking the model to relay the state to
   the user in its first reply, since the user cannot see the block.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh prime
   Done: the line is present whenever prime prints anything at all
3. Files: tests/fixtures/prime/*, tests/fixtures/statusline/
   Action: every prime fixture's expected.txt gains the relay line; add a
   singular-drift statusline case beside the plural one.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: all suites green

## Test plan
The singular cases are the point — the plural ones already pass by accident.

## Boundaries
The relay is one line and asks for one line back. It must not turn into a
session-opening monologue: the status line already carries standing state, and
the block is for the model's orientation first.

title: Statusline names the last completed ticket, not a guess at the next one
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-4).

## Context
FLX-17 made the idle statusline read `FLX-06-unclaimed`, on the principle that
the line should always point at work. Using it says otherwise: the frontier head
is a derived guess, not a fact. It changes when a blocker closes, when a ticket
is filed above it, or when the human decides a lower-numbered blocked ticket
matters more — the FLX-19 → FLX-05 case, where the rule's answer (FLX-06) and
the right answer were different. A statusline that keeps naming a ticket nobody
committed to trains you to ignore it, and it is on screen constantly.

What is idle-time true is what was last finished. It is a fact, not a
projection; it does not move under you; and it answers the question you actually
have in a fresh terminal — where did I get to. The frontier keeps living in
prime's block, where it is shown as a list of several and its uncertainty is
visible.

"Most recent" is the work here. The markdown store has no timestamps, so recency
comes from git: the newest commit message naming a ticket whose status is done —
which is exactly this repo's convention (a ticket ends in a commit carrying its
id). Beads has real close timestamps and should use them. Neither should cost
the statusline anything: this resolves in the hooks, same as `next_ticket` did.

## Tasks
1. Files: bin/flux-common
   Action: add a `store_done` verb returning `id \t title` for the most recently
   completed ticket — beads sorted by close time, markdown resolved through
   `git log`, degrading to the last done ticket in file order outside a repo.
   Move `TICKET_ID_RE` here from bin/flux-prime; both now need it.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh heartbeat
   Done: verb resolves out-of-order completions correctly (FLX-19 after FLX-13)
2. Files: bin/flux-heartbeat, bin/flux-prime, bin/flux-statusline
   Action: replace `next_ticket` with `last_done_ticket` in SESSION_KEYS and in
   both writers; the statusline renders `FLX-19-done` where it rendered
   `FLX-06-unclaimed`, and still `no tickets` when the store has neither a claim
   nor a completion.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: no reader or writer of `next_ticket` remains
3. Files: tests/fixtures/{heartbeat,statusline,prime}/
   Action: retarget the fixtures that pin the frontier head — heartbeat's
   next-ticket case becomes a last-done case with out-of-order commits, and the
   statusline's unclaimed case becomes the done case.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: all suites green, none still asserting on next_ticket
4. Files: README.md, docs/adr/, specs/harness/tickets/05-foundation-checkpoint.md
   Action: correct the README's "always points at work" paragraph and its sample
   lines; record the reversal as an ADR so the next reader does not restore
   `next_ticket` as an oversight; fix FLX-05's check 1, which quotes the old
   `FLX-NN-unclaimed` format.
   Verify: grep -r unclaimed README.md specs/ docs/ returns only the ADR's
   account of the old behaviour
   Done: no document still promises the frontier head in the status line

## Test plan
The heartbeat suite carries the interesting case: a repo whose most recent
ticket commit is not its highest-numbered ticket, proving recency comes from git
rather than from file order.

## Boundaries
Do not touch prime's frontier block — it lists several tickets and shows its own
uncertainty. Do not make the statusline resolve anything itself (FLX-04).

title: SessionStart matcher misses the `fork` source — prime never fires
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-1).

## Context
Found while verifying the `/clear` check during the FLX-05 checkpoint. The
matcher in `hooks/hooks.json` is:

    "matcher": "startup|resume|clear|compact"

The current hooks documentation lists a fifth SessionStart source, `fork`, fired
when a session is forked with `--fork-session`. A forked session therefore starts
with no primed context at all — no claimed ticket, no frontier, no drift — which
is exactly the failure the prime hook exists to prevent, and it fails silently:
there is no error, just an unprimed session that looks normal.

`flux-prime` itself needs no change. It never reads `.source`, and running it
against all five values produces byte-identical output. This is a one-token fix
in the matcher plus a regression test that pins the source list.

## Tasks
1. Files: hooks/hooks.json
   Action: add `fork` to the SessionStart matcher.
   Verify: claude plugin validate . --strict
   Done: matcher reads `startup|resume|clear|compact|fork`
2. Files: tests/ (new case)
   Action: pin the matcher against the documented source list, so a future
   source added upstream fails a test rather than silently skipping prime.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: the test fails when a source is removed from the matcher

## Test plan
The hook script is source-agnostic, so the only thing worth testing is the
matcher string itself — a fixture that asserts the set, not the behaviour.

## Boundaries
Matcher and test only. Do not change flux-prime; it is already correct for every
source. Re-fetch the source list from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks
before writing the test rather than copying it from this ticket — the list is
what changed, and it may have changed again.

title: Statusline is a turn behind a claim made outside a session
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-3, AC-4).

## Context
Found by the human running the claim check during the FLX-05 checkpoint: claim a
ticket, open a new terminal, and prime says `Claimed: FLX-06` while the
statusline still says `FLX-05-unclaimed`. Both are reading honestly — they read
different things:

- prime scans the ticket store on every session start, so it is never stale
- the statusline reads `.flux/session.json`, which only the heartbeat writes
  (spec AC-3), and the heartbeat had not run since the claim

So the first render of every session reflects the *previous* session's last
turn. It self-corrects at the end of the first turn, which is what makes it
nasty: by the time you go looking, it is right. The window is small but it lands
exactly where trust is set — the first thing you see in a new terminal.

This is not the statusline reading the wrong file. Scanning the store on a hook
that fires on every keystroke is the thing FLX-04 deliberately refused (README:
"the frontier head is resolved by the heartbeat, not here"), and that refusal
still stands.

The cheap fix is at the other end: prime already scans the store at SessionStart
and already knows the claim. Have it stamp `claimed_ticket` and `next_ticket`
into `.flux/session.json` before it prints, and the statusline's first render is
correct with no extra work per keystroke. Note this makes prime a second writer
of a file the spec attributes to the heartbeat — deliberate, and worth recording
if it is taken.

Alternative if that is rejected: the statusline treats session.json as stale on
first render and falls back to `no tickets` rather than to a wrong ticket id. A
blank segment is a worse first frame than a correct one, so prefer the stamp.

## Tasks
1. Files: bin/flux-prime (and bin/flux-common if the write belongs there)
   Action: stamp the claim it already resolved into `.flux/session.json`,
   preserving every field it does not own — `last_synced_commit` in particular,
   which only /sync advances.
   Verify: claim a ticket with no session running, run flux-prime, then
   flux-statusline; the statusline names the claimed ticket
   Done: first render after an out-of-session claim is correct (AC-4)
2. Files: bin/flux-prime, hooks + fail-open contract
   Action: keep the write non-fatal — a read-only `.flux/`, absent jq, or
   missing session.json must still leave prime printing its block and exiting 0.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh prime
   Done: prime exits 0 and prints normally with .flux/ unwritable (ADR-0001)
3. Files: tests/fixtures/prime/ (new case), tests/fixtures/statusline/
   Action: fixture for the claim-outside-a-session sequence, and one pinning
   fail-open when the stamp cannot be written.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: both cases fail against today's prime and pass after the fix

## Test plan
The regression is a sequence, not a single invocation: claim → prime → statusline
with no heartbeat in between. The prime suite drives the first two; the assertion
is on what the statusline renders from the session.json prime left behind.

## Boundaries
Do not make the statusline read the ticket store — that is the cost decision
FLX-04 made on purpose. Do not touch `last_synced_commit`; it belongs to /sync
(FLX-14). If prime becomes a writer of session.json, add the ADR rather than
leaving the spec's "session.json (heartbeat)" line silently wrong.

title: Statusline refinements — branch, merged ticket state, token count
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-4, refining the format FLX-04 shipped).

## Context
Raised by the human during the FLX-05 checkpoint, from looking at the real line
rather than the fixtures. Three complaints, all about what the line spends its
width on:

- the worktree/repo name never changes, so it earns nothing — the branch does
- `—` said nothing, and `idle` repeated what an empty ticket segment already said
- a bare percentage does not say how much room is left in absolute terms

New format — the state word folds into the ticket segment, so one segment carries
both the ticket and what is happening to it:

    FLX-04-claimed    · main · ctx 41% · 83.6k
    FLX-11-qualifying · main · ctx 41% · 83.6k   (verb-supplied status)
    FLX-06-unclaimed  · main · ctx 41% · 83.6k   (nothing claimed, frontier head)
    no tickets        · main · ctx 41% · 83.6k   (store has neither)

The interesting constraint is `FLX-06-unclaimed`: naming the frontier head means
knowing the frontier, and FLX-04's boundary forbids the statusline from touching
the store. Resolved by moving the work, not the boundary — the heartbeat already
calls `store_claimed` inside a 500ms budget, so it also caches `next_ticket` into
`.flux/session.json` and the statusline reads it from there. The statusline still
makes no store call and no `git` fork.

## Tasks
1. Files: bin/flux-heartbeat
   Action: cache the frontier head as `next_ticket` in .flux/session.json, via
   `store_ready` (ADR-0002 — never the markdown scan directly).
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh heartbeat
   Done: fixture with a done blocker, a ready ticket and a blocked ticket writes
   `next_ticket: FLX-06`; measured 82ms against the 500ms budget
2. Files: bin/flux-statusline
   Action: branch from .git/HEAD by builtin read (no `git` fork — handles the
   linked-worktree `gitdir:` file, strips refs/heads/, short sha when detached,
   falls back to worktree then directory name); merge status into the ticket
   segment; append `total_input_tokens + total_output_tokens`, formatted 83.6k
   under 100k and 817k above, omitted entirely while zero.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh statusline shellcheck
   Done: 12 fixtures pass, including branch, detached-head, worktree-branch,
   next-unclaimed and tokens-large; measured 20ms against the 100ms budget
3. Files: README.md
   Action: document the four first-segment forms and why the frontier head is
   the heartbeat's job rather than the statusline's.
   Verify: read it against the four fixture expectations
   Done: the documented strings match the fixtures exactly

## Test plan
Five new fixtures (four statusline, one heartbeat) plus every existing statusline
expectation rewritten for the merged label. Both the claimed and unclaimed paths
are covered, as is the no-store case.

## Boundaries
FLX-04's boundary holds and is the reason this ticket is shaped the way it is:
the statusline stays read-only, store-free and fork-free. Anything needing the
ticket store goes in the heartbeat.

## Notes
Done outside the one-ticket-per-session rule (ADR-0003) — written during the
FLX-05 checkpoint session at the human's direction, and recorded here after the
fact so ticket frontmatter stays the only record of progress.

`shellcheck` caught a real bug during the work: `local root="$1" gitdir="$root/.git"`
reads the *caller's* `root`, not the parameter (SC2318). It passed the tests only
because both held the same value.

title: /run — frontier orchestrator over worktree-isolated agents
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-12, user story 6, Out of scope: no auto-retry).

## Context
Built LAST, deliberately: manual mode must feel right first, and native agent teams may absorb parts of this — check https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams for current state before building; prefer native primitives over custom machinery wherever they now reach. A while-loop over the frontier, not a swarm.

## Tasks
1. Files: skills/run/SKILL.md
   Action: flow — (a) frontier from `bd ready` (or the markdown fallback); (b) for each ready ticket up to 3 concurrent: dispatch its routed agent (ticket's `agent:` field → agents/{chore,build,deep}.md) with worktree isolation, the agent following /build's own flow (claim → implement → qualify → close); (c) `checkpoint: human-verify` tickets are never dispatched — the loop stops and presents PAUL's checkpoint format: what was built / how to verify / how to resume; (d) a ticket failing its qualify escalation is tagged with the classification (intent/spec/code) and returned to the frontier as blocked-on-human — no retry; (e) after each completion, recompute the frontier (newly unblocked tickets enter); (f) end when frontier is empty or all remaining tickets are checkpoints/blocked → print a run report table: ticket / agent / result / commit. Completion criterion: "report table row for every ticket the run touched."
   Verify: live-run on 3+ remaining flux tickets with a deliberate checkpoint among them
   Done: parallel worktree execution, checkpoint stop, failure tagging, report — all observed (AC-12)

## Test plan
The live run in Verify, watched via the native agent view. Edge: two tickets touching the same file → worktree isolation prevents the collision; merge order surfaced to the human.

## Boundaries
Concurrency cap 3 is hard in v0.1. /run never merges to main — every branch lands via human diff review. No retry logic (spec: out of scope).

title: Fix TSV row splitting in prime — empty fields collapse
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-2). Bug found while building FLX-04.

## Context
The store verbs in `bin/flux-common` emit tab-separated rows and prime reads them
with `IFS=$'\t' read -r a b c`. That is wrong: tab is IFS *whitespace*, so a run
of tabs counts as one separator and an empty field shifts every later field left.
A ticket whose frontmatter has no `agent` makes prime print the title as the tier:

    FLX-01 [Ticket with no agent field]

instead of `FLX-01 Ticket with no agent field`. Any row with an empty middle
column has the same problem.

Tabs stay the wire format — `@tsv` escapes tabs and newlines inside values, which
a raw separator does not. What changes is how rows are read. `split_row` already
landed in flux-common with FLX-04 (statusline reads its rows through it); prime is
the remaining caller still splitting rows with `read`.

## Tasks
1. Files: bin/flux-prime
   Action: read rows with `IFS= read -r` + `split_row` in all three loops —
   claimed, frontier, handoffs.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh
   Done: a ticket with no `agent` renders `FLX-01 Ticket with no agent field`,
   every existing fixture still passes, shellcheck clean (AC-2)
2. Files: tests/fixtures/prime/missing-agent/
   Action: fixture with one agent-less and one routed open ticket.
   Verify: bash tests/run.sh prime
   Done: fails against the pre-fix prime, passes after — locks the untiered row

## Test plan
Fixtures: prime with an agent-less ticket (new); the whole existing prime,
heartbeat and statusline suites as the regression net.

## Boundaries
Reading only — no change to what the store verbs emit, no new fields, no beads
schema work. Heartbeat's `cut -f1` is already correct; leave it alone.

title: /sync — reconcile off-harness work
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-11, user story 9). ADR-0001 (detection is hook-work; repair is skill-work).

## Context
User-invoked, prompted by prime's drift line. Detection already exists (prime compares `last_synced_commit` from session.json against git log, FLX-02/03); this skill is only the repair. Lazy by design — never blocks, never nags beyond prime's one line. Prime's line offers two endings (`/sync` or `/sync --skip`) and this skill owns both: committing outside the harness on purpose is a legitimate answer, and an offer the tool cannot honour is the failure shape ADR-0010 and FLX-27 were both written about.

## Tasks
1. Files: skills/sync/SKILL.md
   Action: flow — (a) list commits since `last_synced_commit` whose messages match no ticket id; (b) for each cluster of related commits (group by files touched), use gitnexus `detect_changes`/`impact` when available (plain diff reading otherwise) to summarize what changed; (c) create retroactive tickets, already closed, linking the commit shas — history stays queryable, zero ceremony; (d) check the combined changes against `docs/adr/` and CONTEXT.md: flag (never silently rewrite) contradictions with an ADR or glossary term, and raise structural change that no ADR covers as a candidate ADR rather than writing it to a document (ADR-0010); (e) update `last_synced_commit` in .flux/session.json — the only writer of that field besides initialization. `--skip` runs (a) and (e) only: it advances the baseline to HEAD without creating a single ticket, prints which commits it is accepting so the decision is visible, and asks for confirmation first because it is the one path that discards work the harness would otherwise have recorded. It widens what the baseline asserts, from "everything before this is ticketed" to "everything before this is accounted for — ticketed, or deliberately not". Drift accrued after the skip still counts: this silences a specific set of commits, never the check. Completion criterion: "every unattributed commit accounted for in a retroactive ticket — print the commit→ticket table."
   Verify: make two raw commits, run /sync
   Done: retroactive closed tickets exist, drift line gone next session, contradiction check ran; and separately, `--skip` clears the same drift line having created no tickets (AC-11)

## Test plan
Live: raw commits touching (a) a leaf file and (b) something an ADR decides — the second must trigger a flag. Edge: zero drift → /sync says so and exits without writes. Edge: `--skip` on the same two raw commits — drift reads zero next session, `bd list` is unchanged, and a third raw commit afterwards counts as 1 rather than 3.

## Boundaries
Retroactive tickets are always created closed — /sync never reopens work or judges the raw changes. Contradictions with ADRs are flagged for the human, never auto-resolved. `--skip` is never the fallback for a /sync that failed part way: a run that cannot summarize or cannot create tickets stops and says so, because silently advancing the baseline would lose the commits with no record that anything was skipped.
notes: Reconciliation should refresh .beads/issues.jsonl. export.auto is throttled to once a minute after a write, so the tracked escape hatch can lag the database — and a hatch nobody refreshes is worth less than no hatch, because it reads as current. /sync is the right owner: it already walks commits since last_synced_commit, and a hook cannot do it (ADR-0001's <500ms budget, and ADR-0004 forbids the statusline running a store verb).

title: /pause — deposit settled knowledge, write thin handoff
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-10, user story 8).

## Context
User-invoked (also invoked by /plan's budget rule). Two steps in strict order — deposit first, residue second. The handoff must stay thin because everything fat already has a durable home; a handoff that restates a spec section is a bug. flux-prime (FLX-02) already surfaces `.flux/handoffs/*` — this skill only produces the files.

## Tasks
1. Files: skills/pause/SKILL.md, skills/pause/handoff-template.md
   Action: flow — (a) deposit: new glossary terms → CONTEXT.md; decisions meeting the ADR bar (hard to reverse / surprising / real tradeoff) → docs/adr/; agreed spec sections → specs/<slug>/spec-draft.md; (b) residue: write .flux/handoffs/<branch>-<slug>.md from the template — Open questions / Current hypothesis / Next action / Deposited (paths list); (c) tell the user: "paused — /clear or close the terminal; next session will surface this." Completion criterion: "the handoff contains zero facts absent from the Deposited paths — only questions, hypothesis, next action."
   Verify: live pause of a real discussion, then a fresh session
   Done: prime surfaces the handoff; resuming from it recovers the discussion without re-asking settled questions (AC-10)
2. Files: skills/plan/SKILL.md
   Action: replace /plan's inline pause description with an invocation of this skill (single source of truth).
   Verify: /plan at budget invokes /pause
   Done: no duplicated pause instructions anywhere

## Test plan
The live pause/resume cycle in task 1's Verify. Edge: pausing with nothing settled yet (deposit step is a no-op, handoff still valid).

## Boundaries
Handoffs are per-worktree files, gitignored, consumed (archived to .flux/handoffs/done/) on resume. Never write a handoff to the OS temp dir or the repo root.

title: /show-work — diff-scoped behavior diagram artifact
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-9, user story 7).

## Context
User-invoked, takes a ticket id or defaults to the current branch vs merge-base. Claude Code artifacts render mermaid natively (```mermaid in markdown, `<pre class="mermaid">` in HTML) — no infrastructure. The skill is a prompt template with hard conventions; its value is the constraints.

Completion criterion: "every AC in the ticket appears in the checklist as pass/fail with its evidence command."

title: /tickets — spec to routed tickets, fresh window only
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-7, user story 4). ADR-0002, ADR-0003.

## Context
User-invoked. The polluted-window guard is the whole point (ADR-0003): if the session already carries substantial context (heuristic: any prior implementation or long discussion visible in this window), refuse with "run /clear first, then /tickets <spec-path>". Ticket bodies follow the exact format of specs/harness/tickets/ — these files are the living example.

## Tasks
1. Files: skills/tickets/SKILL.md
   Action: flow — (a) guard, then read ONLY the named spec + CONTEXT.md; (b) decompose into tracer-bullet vertical slices, each sized for a single fresh context window; (c) score each ticket's complexity 1-10 → route: ≤3 chore, 4-7 build, ≥8 deep; mark checkpoint: human-verify where only human eyes can judge; (d) declare blockers; quiz the user on granularity and edge cases before writing anything (Matt's to-tickets discipline); (e) create via bd (create + dep add) when available, else numbered markdown files in specs/<slug>/tickets/. Completion criterion: "every user story in the spec is covered by ≥1 ticket, and every ticket names its AC — list the mapping."

title: /build — claim, implement, qualify, close
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-8, user story 5). ADR-0001, ADR-0002.

## Context
User-invoked, takes a ticket id. The four store verbs appear here: claim on start, close on finish (bd when present; else flip the frontmatter `status:` in place). Minimal context load is a hard rule: the ticket, the spec section it names, CONTEXT.md, gitnexus `context` on symbols the ticket names — and nothing else until a task demands it.

## Tasks
1. Files: skills/build/SKILL.md
   Action: flow — (a) claim atomically (`bd update --claim`; markdown fallback: check status is open, set claimed+worktree in one edit); refuse if already claimed elsewhere; (b) load minimal context; (c) implement task-by-task via the installed `/tdd` skill at the seams the ticket pre-agreed; (d) Qualify after every task: re-read actual output, run the Verify command fresh and read its output, compare against the task's Done and the AC it names — never claim from memory; (e) three failed qualify cycles on one task → stop, classify (intent → back to /plan; spec → fix ticket/AC first; code → targeted fix), escalate to the user with the classification; (f) close: commit message references the ticket id, mark done, check the diff against `docs/adr/` (filenames are the index) and CONTEXT.md — new vocabulary may be added to CONTEXT.md, contradictions with an ADR are flagged for the human and never auto-resolved (ADR-0010); offer /show-work. Completion criterion: "every task's Verify command run fresh in this session with output shown — list them."
   Verify: live-run FLX-07 (output style) via /build itself
   Done: dogfood run claims, implements, qualifies, closes with a linked commit (AC-8)

## Test plan
The dogfood run in Verify — /build building a flux ticket is the integration test. Also verify double-claim refusal from a second terminal.

## Boundaries
Respect the ticket's own Boundaries section absolutely — on conflict, stop and escalate (boundary violations are never rationalized). No scope beyond the ticket; discoveries become new tickets (`discovered-from`), not detours.

title: /flux:init — idempotent per-project bootstrap
description:
Spec: specs/harness/spec.md (AC-13, user story 10).

## Context
User-invoked skill (`disable-model-invocation: true`). Behavior ships in the plugin; state is created by /flux:init; nothing is hand-copied. The skill is a checklist where every item is check-then-create — running it twice must change nothing (that IS the verify mode). Read mattpocock-skills `writing-for-agents` before authoring; completion criterion: "every checklist item reported as [exists] or [created] — none skipped."

## Tasks
1. Files: skills/flux:init/SKILL.md
   Action: checklist steps —
   (a) seed CONTEXT.md (empty Language section), docs/adr/, specs/, .flux/ + .gitignore entries
   (b) tooling: jq present? bd present? (`brew install beads` prompt if not) → `bd init` + `bd setup claude` if repo has none
   (c) merge `statusLine` into .claude/settings.json via jq (create file if absent, never clobber other keys)
